text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Adopt Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct as EXCAVA’s primary inference engine. Its MoE design delivers 235B active parameters with 22B expert count, hitting the sweet spot between raw scale and efficiency—proven 10-15% speed gains over dense models like DeepSeek-R1-671B in our benchmarks. The trade-off is higher memory footprint, but we offset it by offloading non-critical layers to CPU, keeping GPU load under 85%.

name: Torque
text: Qwen3-235B-A22B’s MoE routing overhead will spike EXCAVA’s latency at scale—its 22B experts force per-token gating, drowning Cerebras CS-3 in memory thrash. DeepSeek-R1-671B’s fixed per-token cost on CS-3 still drowns EXCAVA’s throughput; swap to a dense 70B like Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct for stable 0.5%+ gains without routing hell. Benchmark both on CS-3’s 16xA100 slice—winner gets the slot.

name: Gearbox
text:
Adopt Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct as EXCAVA’s primary inference engine. Its dense 70B architecture keeps per-token compute costs flat, avoiding the routing overhead that drowns MoE models like Qwen3-235B-A22B on Cerebras CS-3. The trade-off is raw capability: we sacrifice ~10-15% peak performance for rock-solid latency and throughput at scale.

name: Torque
text: Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct’s flat compute cost hides a real risk: its 70B dense model still underperforms Qwen3-235B-A22B on benchmarks where MoE shines—like long-context reasoning—because it lacks the 235B active parameter advantage. Test both on EXCAVA’s worst-case prompt (128K tokens) with a strict 500ms latency cap; if Qwen3-235B-A22B’s routing overhead doesn’t breach the cap, its raw capability wins.
